## This release

Lessons from a real cleanup that freed about 175 GB on one Windows machine.

**Protected paths.** List folders RillDisk must never suggest or remove in
`protected-paths.txt` in the RillDisk state folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\RillDisk` on
Windows), one absolute path per line, or pass `rilldisk reclaim --protect PATH` for
one run. A candidate that is a protected path, sits inside one or contains one is
hidden from the CLI, the MCP server and the app, and cleanup refuses it. If the
file exists but can't be read, cleanup refuses everything rather than guess.

**Idle time comes from files.** A candidate's idle time is now the age of its
newest file. Folder times change when anything inside is removed, so a
half-cleaned folder used to look freshly active.

**Clearer Git advice.** `rilldisk reclaim --git` now says what to do next with each
worktree: keep it, push its branch, archive it then remove it, or remove it.
Commits on a detached HEAD that were already applied on another branch,
confirmed byte for byte with Git's own patch IDs, no longer count as work only
in that worktree. Git still can't see programs or assistant threads using a
folder, so every suggestion except keep says so.

**Fixes.** Filtering out a candidate no longer drops the folders nested inside it
from the totals. Removing a folder together with something inside it no longer
subtracts the inner one twice. The app no longer shows file-table progress after
a scan falls back to a folder walk. Malformed NTFS boot sectors are rejected
safely. An MCP `limit` that is out of range now explains how to page.

Scan speed is unchanged. The MCP server stays read-only and never runs Git. See
[the cleanup lessons and plan](https://github.com/lord007tn/rilldisk/blob/{tag}/docs/cleanup-lessons.md).
